now: Optional synchronous application clock callback returning a numeric time; current implementation snapshots but never invokes it.
Omitted; no application clock callback is invoked.

schedule: Optional synchronous timer adapter receives a no-argument expiry callback and delayMs; returns the opaque handle passed to cancel. A failed scheduler keeps prior semantic identity or gains `CALLBACK_FAILED`; unattachable failures remain on `cause`.

cancel: Optional synchronous timer cancellation receives the original handle returned by schedule; cleanup failure is observed through host `reportError` or terminal host reporting. A reporter failure stays secondary; the frame result is preserved.
Host clearTimeout when available.
Set it when using a custom schedule so completed or closed assemblies release their pending timer. It receives the original opaque handle. Omission uses host clearTimeout when available.

declaredConfiguration.name: chunkBytes
declaredConfiguration.description: Defaults to 16384 units: UTF-16 code units for strings, bytes for Uint8Array messages.

declaredConfiguration.name: maxMessageBytes
declaredConfiguration.description: Defaults to 16777216 units, with the same string/byte distinction as chunkBytes.

declaredConfiguration.name: maxChunks
declaredConfiguration.description: Defaults to 4096 fragments per message; must be a positive safe integer.

declaredConfiguration.name: maxBufferedBytes
declaredConfiguration.description: Defaults to 67108864 retained units across assemblies; at least maxMessageBytes.

declaredConfiguration.name: maxConcurrentMessages
declaredConfiguration.description: Defaults to 256 simultaneous source/message assemblies.

declaredConfiguration.name: assemblyTimeoutMs
declaredConfiguration.description: Defaults to 30000 ms; positive safe-integer retention lifetime for an incomplete assembly.

declaredConfiguration.name: now
declaredConfiguration.description: Retained configuration option; current assembly expiry is driven by schedule, not this clock.

declaredConfiguration.name: schedule
declaredConfiguration.description: Optional timer admission callback; omission uses the host timeout path.

sections.title: 上手

sections.title: 适用场景

sections.content: Use a maintained type example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
id: Application or protocol-owner correlation identifier; preserve it on replies and controls for the same task.
version: Positive component format version chosen by the component owner, independent of package versions.
inputEncodedType: Encoded carrier domain accepted by frame; installation validates codec compatibility.
Arbitrary message-object carrier; no string or byte encoding is imposed.
Text carrier values require a string-compatible codec boundary.
Byte carrier values require an actual Uint8Array encoding.
outputEncodedType: Carrier domain yielded after reassembly, independent from physical fragment objects.
frame: Synchronously partitions one encoded value or returns a whole-frame value when no fragmentation is needed.
frame.value: Encoded message from the matching codec.
frame.context: Transport-owned IRpcFrameContext with actual source and sender-assigned messageId.
Ordered physical frame array; size or fragment-count excess throws FRAME_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
accept: Synchronously admits an ordered fragment or whole carrier into the original source/message assembly.
accept.frame: Received physical whole value or fragment from the matching sender framer.
accept.context: Receiver carrier context with actual source and matching messageId.
IRpcFrameAcceptResult: pending, complete value, or rejected original coded Error.
close: Idempotently closes reassembly, revoking each timer before cancellation so synchronous reentry cancels it once, and drops incomplete messages.
close.reason: Optional caller close reason; built-in framers do not encode or transmit it.
Retained state is released; future receives are rejected where the framer owns terminal state.

symbols.name: IRpcHandshakeFrameReceiver
symbols.signature: export type IRpcHandshakeFrameReceiver = Readonly<{ /** Decode one complete UTF-8 payload; return business text, an admission error, or no delivery. */ accept(frame: Uint8Array): string | Error | undefined; /** Consume the sole handshake frame; repeated reads reject, and close preserves its reason. */ readHandshakeFrame(): Promise<string>; /** Allow the existing post-accept branch while the carrier defers its own consumer activation. */ deferActivation(): void; /** Record responder acceptance before its physical write; throws the retained reason after close. */ beginAccept(): void; /** Enter business-frame decoding after a received control frame; invalid sequencing throws. */ activate(): void; /** Idempotently retain the first reason, reject the reader and drop cached data; owns no I/O. */ close(reason: unknown): void; /** Whether this receiver activated; close does not reset this historical phase flag. */ readonly ready: boolean; }>;
symbols.purpose: Protocol-owned sole handshake wait and UTF-8 phase state, separate from physical connection ownership.
symbols.core:
accept: Decodes one complete payload once; the first text satisfies the sole handshake read, later permitted business text is returned.
accept.frame: Complete native frame payload from the byte decoder, without its length prefix.
Business text, original grammar Error, or undefined while consuming control; invalid UTF-8 is handshake/frame failure by phase, retaining the actual native decoder error on `cause`.
readHandshakeFrame: Consumes the cached first control text or installs exactly one pending reader.
Promise of original control text; duplicate reads reject HANDSHAKE_INVALID, closed reads reject the original close reason.
deferActivation: Allows the original post-accept business handoff before this receiver activates; it does not store an extra physical queue.
Receiver activation remains deferred until activate is called.
beginAccept: Marks the responder actual accept transition before its physical accept write.
Later early-business handling sees acceptance; a closed receiver throws its original reason.
activate: Activates normal business decoding only after an actual first control frame has arrived.
ready becomes true; no received control throws HANDSHAKE_INVALID and closed receivers throw their original reason.
close: Releases the sole reader and cached frame using the first caller-supplied terminal reason.
close.reason: Original connection closure or decode failure supplied by the owning carrier.
Pending and future reads reject the retained original reason; repeated close preserves it.
ready: Whether this receiver has explicitly activated its normal frame phase.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
accept: Decodes one complete payload once; the first text satisfies the sole handshake read, later permitted business text is returned.
accept.frame: Complete native frame payload from the byte decoder, without its length prefix.
Business text, original grammar Error, or undefined while consuming control; invalid UTF-8 is handshake/frame failure by phase, retaining the actual native decoder error on `cause`.
readHandshakeFrame: Consumes the cached first control text or installs exactly one pending reader.
Promise of original control text; duplicate reads reject HANDSHAKE_INVALID, closed reads reject the original close reason.
deferActivation: Allows the original post-accept business handoff before this receiver activates; it does not store an extra physical queue.
Receiver activation remains deferred until activate is called.
beginAccept: Marks the responder actual accept transition before its physical accept write.
Later early-business handling sees acceptance; a closed receiver throws its original reason.
activate: Activates normal business decoding only after an actual first control frame has arrived.
ready becomes true; no received control throws HANDSHAKE_INVALID and closed receivers throw their original reason.
close: Releases the sole reader and cached frame using the first caller-supplied terminal reason.
close.reason: Original connection closure or decode failure supplied by the owning carrier.
Pending and future reads reject the retained original reason; repeated close preserves it.
ready: Whether this receiver has explicitly activated its normal frame phase.

Always supply the complete-payload consumer. It runs synchronously after assembly state is released, and a throw propagates to push(). There is no default consumer.

Return void; callback throws propagate to the decoder caller.

minor: Nonnegative highest compatible minor version; agreement selects the lower shared value.
codec: Negotiated lowercase codec identity selected from both peers’ actual offers.
capabilities: Independent versioned capability declarations; only actual shared offers enable a feature.
peer: Remote diagnostic peer identity retained from the received handshake, without runtime rights.
error: Original or serialized failure carried by this failed result, preserving its causal diagnostics.
versions: Unique supported major versions and each highest compatible minor version, supplied by the application.
codecs: Ordered unique codec identities offered by the application; json is the mandatory baseline.
auth: Optional application portable authentication data; keep tokens out of diagnostic output.
kind: Wire discriminator selected by the producing protocol owner, not by transport or application payload shape.
Treat this record as first-channel negotiation, never business traffic.
step: Selects hello proposal, accept agreement or serialized rejection.
protocol: Exact protocol identity migaia.rpc; unsupported identities cannot complete negotiation.

symbols.signature:
export declare function normalizePortable(value: unknown, depth?: number, active?: Set<object>): IRpcWirePortableValue;

symbols.purpose:
Snapshots supported portable values without sending or executing a request. The default wire domain is null, boolean, finite number, string, array, plain record or a canonical bytes tag; Uint8Array becomes {$rpc: "bytes", base64url}. Records become frozen null-prototype snapshots.

Rejects cycles, nonfinite numbers and unsupported objects with INVALID_ENVELOPE. Ordinary record getters are read once and can execute user code. Native binary belongs to an independently negotiated profile, not the default wire result.
symbols.core:
value: Application or peer value requiring a portable data-only snapshot.
depth: Optional existing traversal depth, default 0 at the root; RPC_PORTABLE_MAX_DEPTH is 64. Ordinary application calls omit this traversal-integration parameter.
active: Optional caller-provided ancestor Set for the same traversal, default undefined with traversal-local cycle tracking. It tracks active ancestors rather than deduplicating all repeated references.
nativeBinary: Optional native-binary branch flag, default false; true admits native bytes, or a synchronous rejection callback supplies the failure boundary.
IRpcWirePortableValue by default, or negotiated IRpcPortableValue with native binary enabled; invalid data throws INVALID_ENVELOPE.

symbols.purpose: Canonical property names for the independent runtime grammar. Each stable key below identifies one wire choice or diagnostic bound.
symbols.core:
profile: Fixed protocol-owned profile marker that separates this grammar from application records.
kind: Wire discriminator selected by the producing protocol owner, not by transport or application payload shape.
id: Application or protocol-owner correlation identifier; preserve it on replies and controls for the same task.
route: Contract-owned routing data kept separate from the application payload.
task: Original runtime task tuple containing mode, caller and exact target generation.
payload: Optional application data admitted through portable normalization, never routing or connection authority.
options: Explicit runtime operation options; absence of a field never infers permission or capability.
steps: Ordered group methods reserved before execution; failure stops later steps without rollback.
operation: Control operation selected by the owning protocol grammar.
reason: Optional serialized cancellation or terminal reason preserving the original failure diagnostics.
stream: Original stream event record carrying its sequence and permitted item or error fields.
completion: Actual original operation success/result or serialized failure, never an execution guess.
idempotencyKey: Application-issued stable operation key reused only when requesting the same business effect.
state: Actual result classification selected by the operation or store owner.
store: Actual final provider store identity and continuity facts, not inferred from a missing key.
outcome: Retained original business completion and target generation from the provider idempotency store.
mode: Original logical operation mode retained across controls and results.
callerId: Caller instance identifier obtained from the actual runtime peer identity.
callerGeneration: Caller-owned generation obtained from its actual accepted runtime identity.
targetGeneration: Exact target generation obtained from the accepted provider binding and preserved across controls.
method: Application method name chosen from the provider or remote contract being invoked.
value: Generation owner-issued nonnegative safe integer, not a supervisor attempt ordinal.
providerId: Identifier issued by the generation owner and obtained from the accepted provider binding.
orderKey: Application-issued ordering lane key; the final provider owns arrival ordering for equal keys.
cancel: Explicit before-start cancellation policy selected by the original caller.
timeoutMs: Optional relative operation deadline in integer milliseconds from `0` through `2147483647`; zero is allowed.
ok: Boolean discriminator separating successful completion from serialized failure.
result: Portable business result present only when the associated completion or step succeeds.
error: Original or serialized failure carried by this failed result, preserving its causal diagnostics.
event: Protocol-owned discriminator for the selected runtime semantic variant.
seq: Nonnegative stream sequence owned by the stream protocol; initial open uses zero.
epoch: Original idempotency-store incarnation identifier issued by the store owner.
continuity: Original store owner-issued continuity fact, never inferred from a missing key.
parameters: This const declaration has no parameters.

symbols.signature: export declare function checkRpcRuntimeStreamFinish(options: Pick<IRpcRuntimeOptions, 'cancel'>): Error | undefined;
symbols.purpose: Validates finish-without-items against actual call options; only before-start cancellation permits this finish control.
symbols.core:
options: Actual original call cancel option, not a reconstructed capability claim.
Undefined when allowed; invalid finish returns a coded INVALID_STREAM Error without mutating ownership.
cancel: Only before-start requests final-provider cancellation arbitration before execution begins.
Absent: ordinary cancellation keeps its existing owner.
The final provider decides cancellation before its actual execution start.
Pass the original task cancel option when validating finish-without-items. before-start admits that control; omission rejects it. These helpers only return the validation error and never cancel or drain a producer.

symbols.purpose: Snapshot of bounded fragment-retention policy captured by each fragment framer constructor.
symbols.core:
chunkBytes: Positive safe-integer fragment size: bytes for binary, UTF-16 code units for strings; cannot exceed maxMessageBytes.
`16384` units per fragment.
maxMessageBytes: Positive safe-integer size ceiling for complete inbound/outbound values and reassembly; string counts UTF-16 code units, binary counts bytes. Cannot exceed maxBufferedBytes.
`16777216` encoded units per message.
maxChunks: Positive safe-integer maximum declared fragments for one message.
`4096` fragments per message.
maxBufferedBytes: Positive safe-integer total retained incomplete data across all source/message pairs.
`67108864` retained encoded units.
maxConcurrentMessages: Positive safe-integer maximum simultaneous incomplete source/message assemblies.
`256` concurrent incomplete messages.
assemblyTimeoutMs: Positive safe-integer timer deadline after the first fragment before marking its assembly expired.
`30000` milliseconds from first fragment.
now: Optional synchronous application clock callback returning a numeric time; current implementation snapshots but never invokes it.
Omitted; no application clock callback is invoked.
Supply only when sharing a framer configuration shape that already includes a clock. Current assembly expiry retains this callback but never invokes it; omission has the same expiry behavior. Use schedule to control expiry.
schedule: Optional synchronous timer adapter receives a no-argument expiry callback and delayMs; returns the opaque handle passed to cancel. A failed scheduler keeps prior semantic identity or gains `CALLBACK_FAILED`; unattachable failures remain on `cause`.
Host setTimeout when available; no timer when the host lacks it.
Set it when the carrier owns a timer queue. Return one handle for the expiry callback; cancel receives that handle. Omission uses host setTimeout when available, otherwise no timer is armed.
cancel: Optional synchronous timer cancellation receives the original handle returned by schedule; cleanup failure is observed through host `reportError` or terminal host reporting. A reporter failure stays secondary; the frame result is preserved.
Host clearTimeout when available.
Set it when using a custom schedule so completed or closed assemblies release their pending timer. It receives the original opaque handle. Omission uses host clearTimeout when available.
